items.review_rationale: Reviewed the full eventual-stabilization condition for images of inverse-system transition maps: for each i there exists j≥i such that all later images at i coincide. This is a Mittag-Leffler property of systems of sets and is not the tensor-comparison Mittag-Leffler property of modules.

references.phrase: for every i exists j≥i for all k≥j
references.disposition: The stabilizing index may depend on i; equality is of images in A_i, not equality of transition maps.

items.review_rationale: Read the unique-lift property for every square-zero ideal I of any R-algebra A, preserving both existence and uniqueness of a compatible lift S→A. Formally étale is stronger than only formally unramified, and this is not simply the finite-presentation étale condition.

references.context: Commutative algebra: square-zero ideal with vanishing ideal product I²
Commutative algebra: quotient R-algebra of A by ideal I

references.phrase: unique compatible lifting S→A of S→A/I
references.context: Deformation theory: a uniquely determined lift of an R-algebra homomorphism through a square-zero quotient

references.phrase: every R-algebra A and ideal I
references.disposition: The source quantifies over all such square-zero extensions, not only split or finite ones.

items.review_rationale: Read the construction of scheme base change as a fibre product over S with projection to S′; the new scheme is not simply the Cartesian product of underlying topological spaces.

references.disposition: The canonical projection is part of the fibre-product structure, not an arbitrary chosen map.

items.review_rationale: Read universal stability of a relative scheme property P under arbitrary base change, retaining the quantifier over all S′→S and the induced base-changed morphism.

references.phrase: P is preserved for every S′→S
references.disposition: The criterion is a logical preservation property of P, not a separate assertion that every property of morphisms is stable.

items.review_rationale: Read the scheme fibre at a point s: it is the base change along Spec(κ(s))→S, retains nilpotent scheme structure, and is considered over κ(s), not just the set-theoretic preimage f^{-1}(s).

references.context: Algebraic geometry: residue field at a scheme point via quotient of the stalk by its maximal ideal

references.disposition: The fibre is taken at the given scheme point, not a generic geometric point with an algebraic-closure choice.

items.review_rationale: Read inertia objects (x,α) with α a vertical automorphism over identity of p(x), and morphisms intertwining those automorphisms. This is not an arbitrary arrow category nor the relative inertia of a separate functor F.

references.phrase: automorphism α of x over identity of p(x)
references.context: Category theory: vertical invertible endomorphism of object in a fibred category
Category theory: arrows β with β∘α=α′∘β over the base projection

references.disposition: Automorphisms are vertical in the fibre; ordinary arrows not preserving base are excluded from the automorphism condition.

items.review_rationale: Read the relative inertia condition for the functor F:S→S′: automorphism α of x must become the identity of F(x), not merely an arbitrary vertical automorphism or an automorphism whose image is invertible.

references.phrase: kernel of automorphism mapping F on an object
references.context: Category theory: vertical automorphisms mapped to identity by a fibred functor

references.disposition: This exact identity condition is stricter than preserving automorphisms under F.

items.review_rationale: Read N-2/Japanese relative to the fraction field K of an integral domain R. For each finite field extension L/K the integral closure inside L must be finite as an R-module; not just integral, not only normal in K, and not a field with finitely many elements.

references.phrase: integral closure of R in L

references.disposition: Finite refers to field extension degree; the module-finiteness of the integral closure is a further required condition.
